# The type and nullability of every property reachable from the external contract set.
#
# REQ-API-009's last open acceptance box, closed 2026-09-10 (ADR-0161 8.4). ADR-0136 names the gap
# itself: ExternalContractTest "does not compare types, nullability or enum values. A field that
# turns from string to object, or an enum that loses a constant, passes it and still breaks an old
# build." Enums were closed first; this is the other half.
#
# FORMAT  Schema.property=signature, one per line, sorted, generated by
# ExternalContractTest#theContractTypesAndNullabilityAreFrozen when it fails.
#
#   string, boolean, number          a bare JSON type
#   string/uuid, integer/int64       type/format
#   array<string>, array<$MissionDto>  an array and what it holds
#   $SquadronReferenceDto            a $ref to another schema
#   trailing !                       the schema lists this property as REQUIRED
#
# WHY `!` AND NOT `nullable`. This document carries no `nullable` keyword and no ["string","null"]
# type union -- springdoc emits neither, at OpenAPI 3.1. Membership of a schema's `required` list
# is therefore the whole of the nullability signal the contract has, and freezing it is what makes
# "a field stopped being required" a build failure instead of a null on a member's phone.
#
# A DATA FILE RATHER THAN A LITERAL. FROZEN_REQUIRED_ENUMS is a Map.ofEntries in the test, and this
# is not: at 1,479 entries the literal would be longer than the test around it, and a change to the
# contract is far easier to review as a sorted data diff than as a diff of Java. The guarantee is
# the same -- the file is committed, and changing it is a deliberate act in the same PR.
#
# CHANGING AN ENTRY IS A CONTRACT CHANGE. A shipped Android build cannot be redeployed with the
# server. If a type here has to move, ship an app build that accepts the new one FIRST.
